text: Bank memos beginning with or containing 'UPWORK *CONTRACTOR' are Upwork, a professional services vendor. Categorize these transactions as 'Professional Services'. These appear as debits (money out) on the operating account.

title: Example: Upwork
text: Example transaction: a debit with description 'UPWORK *CONTRACTOR' for a few hundred to a few lakh rupees should be booked to 'Professional Services'. The exact amount is verified against the bank feed, never inferred.

title: Channel deposit: Razorpay → Razorpay Sales
text: Bank deposits with memo 'RAZORPAY SETTLEMENT' are settlement payouts from the Razorpay payment gateway and are categorized as 'Razorpay Sales' (revenue). These are credits (money in), and the bank memo carries a UTR that also appears on the settlement report — use it as the primary join key.

title: Reconciliation policy: Razorpay
text: Razorpay batches many orders into a periodic settlement. The bank only sees the NET amount: gross sales minus the gateway fee (~2.0%) minus GST on that fee (~18% of the fee, not of gross) minus refunds (~3.5%). To reconcile, recompute net = gross − (fee + GST-on-fee) − refunds from the Razorpay settlement report and match it to the bank deposit to the penny, using the shared UTR. Settlements land ~2 business day(s) after the transaction, so match within a date window, not on an exact date.

title: Reconciliation policy: Razorpay risk hold
text: Razorpay may place a settlement under risk/compliance review, so a bank deposit can be SHORT of the computed net settlement. Do not force-match these; flag the shortfall as a risk hold and reconcile the released amount in a later period.

title: Razorpay fees policy
text: Razorpay gateway fees (plus GST charged on the fee) are netted out of settlements. Record the fee portion to 'Razorpay Fees' (COGS) so gross revenue and fees are both visible, rather than only booking the net deposit.

title: Payroll: net pay vs statutory dues
text: A 'RAZORPAYX PAYROLL NET DIRECT DEP' debit is net wages paid to employees → 'Payroll Expense'. A separate 'RAZORPAYX PAYROLL EPF CHALLAN' debit is the employer's EPF contribution → 'Payroll Taxes'. They are two distinct postings from one payroll run.

title: Refunds & chargebacks
text: Refunds and chargebacks are contra-revenue: they reduce the related channel's revenue rather than being booked as an expense.

title: Internal transfers are not P&L
text: 'TRANSFER TO/FROM SAVINGS' movements between the company's own accounts are internal transfers, not income or expense, and must be excluded from the P&L.

title: Owner distributions
text: 'OWNER DISTRIBUTION' / draws are equity movements, not operating expenses, and do not appear on the income statement.

title: Edge case: Razorpay subscription vs Razorpay settlement
text: Beware: 'RAZORPAY SOFTWARE SUBS' is a debit for the company's OWN Razorpay platform subscription (an expense, Office & Admin), whereas 'RAZORPAY SETTLEMENT' is a credit PAYOUT of collected customer payments (Razorpay Sales revenue). Both memos start with 'RAZORPAY' — the direction of the amount (debit vs credit) disambiguates them, not the memo prefix alone.
